sourcesChecked.name: Internet Archive items credited to Miniclip
sourcesChecked.about: Preserved game items on the Internet Archive whose creator field names Miniclip (searched with the archive.org advanced search API; only the item metadata was read, no game files were downloaded). Items from the numbered "casa" collection carry exact dates (year= below). Other upload dates are often just the upload year and are NOT used as release years. dev= is only given when the item credits a developer.

sourcesChecked.name: Maintainer's audit checklist (2026)
sourcesChecked.about: Titles the project maintainer asked the 2026 audit to check and to add when missing. Spellings as supplied; "T. or Treat Smash" is the shortened "Trick or Treat Smash" and "Mystic Mermaid Pin" the shortened "Mystic Mermaid Pinball".

sourcesChecked.name: Maintainer's master list
sourcesChecked.about: The 752-title list of classic Miniclip games supplied by the project maintainer, compiled from several historical Miniclip game lists (2007, 2008-2009 and 2010). Spellings are kept exactly as supplied - duplicate or shortened spellings are merged into one record by the catalogue tools.

sourcesChecked.name: Miniclip Arcade (classic.miniclip.com)
sourcesChecked.about: Miniclip's own classic Flash games archive, run with the Ruffle emulator. Its game list (https://classic.miniclip.com/games.json) names 16 games. The files are served by Miniclip with "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *", so these games can be STREAMED from Miniclip's server into this site's Ruffle player - nothing is copied into this repository. play= is the official SWF address, size= the stage size read from the SWF header. id= points the entry at the catalogue record it belongs to.

sourcesChecked.name: Miniclip CD "Ultimate Game Pack" (Christmas 2006)
sourcesChecked.about: Miniclip's own offline games CD. Titles are taken from the CD's menu (index.htm) and its game pages; where the menu and the game page spell a title differently both spellings are kept (aka=). Only the file LISTING of the CD was read - no game files were downloaded.

sourcesChecked.name: Miniclip offline game downloads (early 2000s)
sourcesChecked.about: Miniclip offered many early games as self-contained Windows downloads named "Miniclip Game <title>.exe". The Internet Archive item "66 Offline EXE Old Miniclip games" preserves them; only its file LISTING was read. Files in that collection WITHOUT the "Miniclip Game" prefix (Elf Bowling, Pacman, Desktop Destroyer...) are other companies' games and are NOT used as evidence. "abduction.exe" is the same download as "Miniclip Game Alien Abduction.exe" and "paintball.exe" the same as "Miniclip Game Stress Relief Paintball.exe".

sourcesChecked.name: Candidates rejected by the audit
sourcesChecked.about: Titles that turned up while researching but are NOT added to the catalogue. The archive covers Miniclip's web games from 2001 to 2012. reason= says why each one was left out. Kept here so the next audit does not re-add them by mistake.

sourcesChecked.name: Game databases and wikis
sourcesChecked.about: Facts (mostly release years and developers) found in game databases, encyclopedias and fan wikis through web searches during the 2026 audit. ref= names where the fact came from; each ref counts as its own source. Only facts that were stated plainly are used - where two sources disagree the year stays empty (see conflicts at the bottom).

sourcesChecked.name: Miniclip homepage screenshots (2008-2009)
sourcesChecked.about: The four screenshots of the 2008-2009 Miniclip homepage this site was rebuilt from. Titles are transcribed from what is legible: the Latest Games, Hot Games and Top Ten panels, the six category boxes and the parts of the Full Games List that are visible (the list is cut off in the screenshots, so most titles are NOT visible - absence here means nothing). Spellings are exactly as shown.

sourcesChecked.name: Miniclip Shockwave games collection
sourcesChecked.about: A preservation collection of Miniclip's Shockwave (Director) games, credited to Miniclip. Only the file LISTING was read. Where the archive file name credits a developer ("... - Silent Bay Studios") it is given as dev=. Titles from 2013 and later are left out here and listed in out-of-era.txt instead.

sourcesChecked.name: Uncertain variants - decisions
sourcesChecked.about: Spellings that COULD be the same game as a catalogue record (or not), and what the audit decided. merged = kept as an alias of the record; separate = kept as its own record; not-added = left out until better evidence turns up. Not evidence - notes for the next audit.

sourcesChecked.name: Web search - miniclip.com game pages
sourcesChecked.about: Titles checked with a web search during the 2026 catalogue audit. Each one turned up an old miniclip.com game page address (www.miniclip.com/games/<slug>/<lang>/, or the same address on Miniclip's site., sapo., fungames. and sandbox. mirrors) in the search results, which shows the game was hosted on Miniclip. The pages themselves could not be opened (the Wayback Machine and most sites were unreachable from the audit machine), so this counts as one independent source, not as direct proof. page= is the slug that was found; year=/dev= only where the result said so.
